text: Git branching is a powerful way to manage changes in a project without disrupting the main code. In a typical workflow, developers create a *feature branch* to work on a new idea or fix. This branch is a separate copy of the code, so you can experiment freely. Once your work is complete, you *merge* it back into the main branch. Before merging, however, many teams use *pull requests* to review the changes and discuss any issues. This process, known as version control workflow, keeps the project organized and reduces errors. By using branches, you ensure that the main version always remains stable while new features are developed safely.
